predecessors.name: Prince Bishopric of Sion
predecessors.text: the Upper Valais, over which 'In 999, King Rudolph III of Burgundy gave all temporal rights and privileges to the Bishop of Sion'

successors.name: Helvetic Republic
successors.text: the Valais, 'incorporated as the canton of Valais of the Helvetic Republic' in 1798, Upper and former Lower Valais together

ledger.x: 1416: the Sieben Zenden ally with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne.
1416: the Upper Valais (Sieben Zenden) becomes a Zugewandter Ort (associate) of the Confederacy.
November 1475: the Zenden seize the Savoyard Lower Valais.
November 1475: the Lower Valais up to Martigny becomes the associate's land.
March 1476: the Zenden take Saint-Maurice, Monthey, Évian and Thonon.
March 1476: Saint-Maurice and Monthey town join the associate's land (the Swiss tint of swiss-confederation /ledger/15 already covers this cell from November 1475, on a wider circle).
March 1476: the Monthey district's northern part joins the associate's land, to be lost in 1477 and regained in 1536 with Monthey.
1477: the Zenden give up Évian, Thonon and Monthey.
1477: the Monthey district's northern cell leaves the associate's land with the loss above.
1536: the Zenden win Évian, Thonon and Monthey again.
1536: the Monthey district's northern cell is the associate's land again, with the regain above.
1569: the Zenden keep Monthey and give back Évian and Thonon.
1634: the prince-bishop gives up secular power for good.
16 March 1798: the Valais becomes a single republic.
March 1798: the Upper Valais ceases to be an associate of the Confederacy.
March 1798: the Lower Valais up to Martigny ceases to be the associate's land.
March 1798: Saint-Maurice and Monthey town end as associate land with the Confederacy.
March 1798: the Monthey district's northern cell ends as associate land with the Confederacy.
1798: the Valais joins the Helvetic Republic.
1 May 1798: the republic of the Valais ends.

wars.name: Raron affair
wars.outcome: The Canton of Valais page dates the rebellion 1414 to 1420; Lucerne, Uri and Unterwalden backed the Upper Valais rebels and Bern backed the Rarons.

wars.name: Savoyard Lower Valais and Chablais campaigns
wars.outcome: The Zenden seized the Lower Valais up to Martigny in November 1475 and Saint-Maurice, Évian, Thonon and Monthey in March 1476; they gave up the last three districts in 1477 and won them again in 1536; by the treaty of Thonon of 1569 Monthey, Val-d'Illiez and…

certainty.note: Valley jurisdictions; the Morge frontier of 1416-1474 and the Lower Valais and Chablais boundaries after 1475 are cell readings of the places the Canton of Valais page names (Martigny, Saint-Maurice, Monthey, Évian, Thonon), not surveyed…
